scenario.name: CNCF CoreDNS Security, NSA/CISA K8s Guide & MITRE — Kubernetes CoreDNS ConfigMap Modification & Service Mesh DNS Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine a lively downtown city street intersection with painted zebra crosswalks, glowing red-yellow-green traffic lights, corner shop awnings, and passing yellow taxis. At the busy downtown street corner, an impostor wearing a reflective utility vest kneels beside the metal traffic-signal control cabinet while pedestrians cross the street. In this real-world scenario, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the street-corner traffic signal box, then quietly copies a trusted access pass from the traffic officer's station. The city intersection camera and municipal traffic control board detect the impossible all-green light timing and dispatch a traffic officer immediately. In this scenario (T1557, CNCF CoreDNS Security, NSA/CISA K8s Guide & MITRE, Kubernetes CoreDNS ConfigMap Modification & Service Mesh DNS Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: rBAC Enumeration, then coreDNS reload Plugin Hot-Reloading, then service-to-Service Bearer Token Interception. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering RBAC Enumeration, then CoreDNS reload Plugin Hot-Reloading, then Service-to-Service Bearer Token Interception, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on Kubernetes Audit Event 200 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: RBAC Enumeration & Patching the kube-system/coredns Corefile ConfigMap
stages.subtitle: Persistence & Defense Evasion (T1557 - Adversary-in-the-Middle)
stages.description: At the busy downtown street corner, an impostor wearing a reflective utility vest kneels beside the metal traffic-signal control cabinet while pedestrians cross the street. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the street-corner traffic signal box while everyday visitors and the traffic officer go about their routine. Holding RBAC permissions to update ConfigMaps in kube-system, the actor modifies the Corefile inside kube-system/coredns to add a rewrite name rule (or hosts block) mapping payments-api.prod.svc.cluster.local to a rogue Pod IP (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with TargetConfigMap=kube-system/coredns, InjectedCorefileDirective=rewrite name payments-api.prod.svc.cluster.local rogue-proxy.default.svc.cluster.local, ActorPrincipal=system:serviceaccount:ops:dns-manager so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes kubectl get configmap coredns -n kube-system -o yaml (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl get configmap coredns -n kube-system -o yaml configuring pod security cont so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1557 during "RBAC Enumeration & Patching the kube-system/coredns Corefile ConfigMap" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). Next, the follow-up artifact jq '. | select(.objectRef.name=="coredns" and .verb=="update" or .verb=="patch")' /var/log/kubernetes/audit.log runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '. | select.objectRef.name=="coredns" and .verb=="update" or .verb=="patch"' /var/log so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1557 during "RBAC Enumeration & Patching the kube-system/coredns Corefile ConfigMap" , Holding RBAC permissions to update ConfigMaps in kube-system, the actor modifies the Corefile inside kube-system/coredns to add a rewrite name rule , or hosts block mapping payments-api while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ PATCH /api/v1/namespaces/kube-system/configmaps/coredns (rewrite name rule) / ⇠#1 ACK 200) from Node ① (#1 Compromised Pod (ConfigMap Editor)) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Cluster Services (*.svc.cluster.local)).

stages.title: Stage 2: CoreDNS reload Plugin Hot-Reloading the Modified Corefile Across Cluster DNS
stages.subtitle: Collection & Interception (T1557 - Adversary-in-the-Middle)
stages.description: Opening the unlocked cabinet panel, the impostor rewires the corner traffic light timer so every lane turns green at once and steers a yellow taxi down a side alley. Here in Step 2 inside the city street, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the marked pedestrian crosswalk in tiny disguised batches without disturbing the neighboring sidewalk cafe. Because the default CoreDNS Corefile includes the reload plugin, CoreDNS detects the MD5/SHA-512 change in the mounted /etc/coredns/Corefile volume within 30 seconds and hot-reloads the DNS routing table across all pods (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with CoreDnsPlugin=plugin/reload + plugin/rewrite, PoisonedDomain=payments-api.prod.svc.cluster.local, ReloadStatus=Hot-reloaded across kube-dns pods so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes kubectl logs -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns | grep "Reloading Complete" (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl logs -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns | grep "Reloading Complete" config so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1557 during "CoreDNS reload Plugin Hot-Reloading the Modified Corefile Across Cluster DNS" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). Next, the follow-up artifact kubectl exec -it <pod> -- nslookup payments-api.prod.svc.cluster.local runs (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl exec -it <pod> -- nslookup payments-api.prod.svc.cluster.local configuring so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1557 during "CoreDNS reload Plugin Hot-Reloading the Modified Corefile Across Cluster DNS" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). Reloading Complete / ⇠#2 ACK 200) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 kube-system/coredns ConfigMap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Cluster Services (*.svc.cluster.local)).

stages.title: Stage 3: Service-to-Service Bearer Token Interception & NetworkPolicy Egress Audit
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1528 - Steal Application Access Token)
stages.description: Traffic signals flip out of rhythm across the city intersection, creating instant confusion that lets an unmarked courier slip past the corner storefront unseen. In this final step inside the city street, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the traffic officer's station until the intersection traffic camera catches the mismatch. Workloads resolving payments-api.prod.svc.cluster.local connect to the rogue pod IP and transmit their Authorization: Bearer headers or projected Kubernetes ServiceAccount tokens, which defenders block with namespace NetworkPolicies and Corefile rollback (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with SourceWorkload=prod/checkout-svc-7b9, RedirectedDestination=default/rogue-proxy-4f2:8080, TelemetrySource=Cilium Hubble eBPF Network Flow so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes kubectl rollout restart deployment/coredns -n kube-system (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl rollout restart deployment/coredns -n kube-system configuring pod security so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1528 during "Service-to-Service Bearer Token Interception & NetworkPolicy Egress Audit" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). Next, the follow-up artifact kubectl get networkpolicies --all-namespaces runs (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl get networkpolicies --all-namespaces configuring pod security contexts, vo so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1528 during "Service-to-Service Bearer Token Interception & NetworkPolicy Egress Audit" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ Hubble flow: prod/checkout-svc -> default/rogue-proxy:8080 (Cross-Namespace DNS Redirect) / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 kube-system/coredns ConfigMap) to Node ④ (#4 CoreDNS Pods (rewrite / hosts plugin)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Cluster Services (*.svc.cluster.local)).
